text:
maria: hey — weird one. noticed ~6 sessions still hitting canary after we rolled it back 15m ago. small sample but stable users. anyone seen sticky + header routing oddities recently?
aj: hmm, can you paste a sample request header/cookie?
maria: pasted sanitized example: `Cookie: _rd_sticky=abc123; session=v2d9` and `x-deploy-route: stable` but traces show request -> canary.
samir: interesting, our routing order is supposed to check guards (header) before sticky. if header says stable we short-circuit, sticky shouldn't win.
kai: could be hash key collision — sticky hashing uses `session` key, but we also compute route-hash using `x-deploy-route` for split buckets in some legacy codepaths. if the header was set but empty earlier it might have seeded the bucket.
maria: here's the rollout config for that service from the console:```yaml
rollout:
  mode: canary
  split: 0.02
  guards:
    - type: header
      name: x-deploy-route
      value: stable
    - type: cookie
      name: _rd_sticky
      key: session
```
aj: that looks fine. if header-guard matched stable we should not consult cookie. do we have telemetry showing guard-eval order?
samir: telemetry shows a couple of events where `guard_eval_order` was `cookie,header` (unexpected). looks like older agent versions flip order when a feature flag `enable_cookie_optim` is on.
olivia: ugh that flag was toggled last week to reduce cookie parsing CPU on high qps paths.
kai: so we probably hit a race: some edge proxies running old routing-agent had new flag off (header-first), new agents had flag on (cookie-first) — mix in sticky persistence and you get users pinned to previous target despite header change.
maria: makes sense. do we have an easy repro? I can run a small harness setting header+cookie combos.
aj: yes, can you run curl loop toggling `x-deploy-route` and replay the same sticky cookie across requests? that should reproduce.
maria: repro done, attaching condensed logs: `req1 header=stable cookie=abc -> canary` `req2 header=stable cookie=abc -> canary` `req3 header=stable cookie=xyz -> stable`
samir: confirms cookie-first behavior when flag enabled. fix options: 1) revert flag globally, 2) change routing-agent to always respect guard precedence (header before cookie) at protocol level, 3) add telemetry that asserts guard ordering and raise alert.
olivia: ops prefers config toggle rollback for immediate mitigation. can we do that safely?
kai: yes, takeover window is small. but we should also ship the agent fix so this doesn't recur when the toggle is re-enabled.
aj: agree. also need console UX change: show effective guard evaluation order on rollout config page and a badge when mixed agent versions exist in the cluster. people are relying on implicit ordering.
maria: filed issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/3452 (sticky-header-ordering) with steps, repro, and suggested fix. adding owners: @aj, @kai, @samir.
deploy-bot: Canary was rolled back for service 'kb-encoder' at 2225003400 :white_check_mark:
kai: after rollback, we'll rollout agent fix to canary group, run the harness for 10k reqs, then gradually enable cookie-optim.
aj: i'll add a telemetry check to compare `declared_guard_order` vs `runtime_guard_order` and alert on mismatch.
maria: thanks all — marking this thread for follow-up in tomorrow standup. :thumbsup:
